derivedFrom: the two registered evaluators' own rules, worked by hand over the name-nights below rather than read back from a run. The index reading fires where the relative strength index is at or below the registered level, inclusive at the level, which is why two of the cases sit exactly on it and one a hundredth above. The histogram turn fires where the previous session's histogram was at or below zero and tonight's is at or above the registered margin, which is a fact about two sessions and not one, so the case that sits above zero on both nights does not fire however high it is. The name-nights are constructed rather than taken from the committed fixture, and the reason is stated rather than left as a choice: over four names of real bars every one of them fires a live reason, so the fixture cannot supply the name-night this is most about, which is one no live reason surfaced.

overTheReplayedNight.derivedFrom: the shadow column's rules worked by hand over the replayed fixture with six constructed members added, rather than read back from a run, and put to the builder through a store so the register read, the instant, the two sessions an evaluator is handed, the refusal of a stale or gapped name and the two lists are each reached. A candidate stands for the night if it was registered before the night started, so the one registered five minutes after the night's start and ten before the stage's is evaluated nowhere. The index reading at a level of one hundred fires wherever it is evaluated, because the relative strength index lies between 0 and 100; on the four fixture names it is evaluated on every row, since each holds 252 sessions and the reading's warm-up is 14. The histogram turn on a fixture name fires where its own two newest stored histograms say so, recomputed by the test from the indicator rows rather than written here. A name with no bar for the session, or with a hole in its stored series, is skipped by every candidate with the reason its row carries and its readings are never read, whatever they hold; a reading not available is skipped by the candidate that reads it and no other. Evaluations and skips together are the standing candidates times the members, 2 times 10, which is 14 evaluations and 6 skips, and none of the six skips fails the stage. A candidate registered under an evaluator version the code does not carry is the one skip that does: it is skipped on all 10 rows, named once on the stage's line, and leaves the other counts as they were.
